coldRead.icp: CEO/administrator of a 25-bed Critical Access Hospital in rural Texas, not a finance or policy specialist, who heard there is state rural-health grant money and wants to know if their hospital is getting any and what to do; reading once, start to finish

undefinedTerms: first budget period / Budget Period 1 (when it started is never said)
first-year award vs first-year money (two different totals, near-identical wording)
pendency of the contract execution process
mondayActions: Search HHSC's October 23 list for our hospital name, hospital district, county and operating company
Read the 'Awarded (Contract Fully Executed)' column on each of our rows
Ask whoever signs contracts for us whether an HHSC contract is waiting on our side
Leave any unsigned (No) row out of next quarter's staffing and hiring plan
Set a weekly calendar reminder to re-check the HHSC list
Before spending a signed award on people, read the linked nurse-salary rules article
blockedActions: See my own hospital's row in the article: no per-hospital table, and Step 1 does not link the .xlsx (the methodology notes HHSC's server refused a direct download, so it may not open for me either)
Tell whether my unsigned money is at risk on October 30: the article says HHSC has not said
Find out whether I can still apply: Initiatives 2, 3 and 5 have no rows, but the article never says whether they are open, closed or coming
Know whom to call at HHSC about a stuck contract: no contact or office named
Know whether my hospital is one of the 18 matched only through an inferred owner, i.e. whether the rows the article counts for me are really mine

sections.heading: Key Takeaways
sections.notes: 31% (bullet 2) then 'stayed near 39%' (bullet 4) with no denominator change flagged: reader thinks one number is wrong. '$281,319,360.67 first-year award' penny precision in a takeaway. The CAH bullet (86 of 92) is the reader's hook but it is last.

sections.heading: What Does Intent to Award Mean for a Rural Texas Strong Grant?
sections.notes: Clear first two sentences. 'during the pendency of the contract execution process' inside the quote. 'Year 1 subset' admitted as undefined.

sections.heading: How Much Rural Texas Strong Money Is Under Signed Contract?
sections.notes: Opens with '$87,432,868.65'. Initiative-name paragraph (six names, three absent) and the 'our reading of HHSC's program page' label caveat are methodology the CEO does not need. 'first-year money' ($223.0M listed) vs 'first-year award' ($281.3M) are two near-identical phrases for different totals.

sections.heading: Is Rural Texas Strong Money Being Signed Faster Than It Is Being Listed?
sections.notes: Attention starts dropping here; this is about the state's paperwork pace, not the reader's hospital. 'Signing has kept pace with the list but has not caught up with it' reads as contradictory next to +$36.4M signed vs +$93.9M listed. 'On October 8 the signed share of the $281.3 million award was lower, because the list itself was shorter. A rising share of the award tells you the list is growing. It does not tell you contracts are catching up.' needed three passes.

sections.heading: What Was the $8 Million Rural Texas Strong Announcement on October 22?
sections.notes: Answer is clear (one weekly batch). Date juggling: added Oct 14, announced Oct 22, checked Oct 23. '$23,955,761.64' all-years figure is one number too many.

sections.heading: Do the Rural Texas Strong Announcements Match the State's Recipient List?
sections.notes: Reader abandons linear reading here and jumps to the CAH section / What to Do. Four-column table of budget lines to the cent. 'Keep them apart if you quote either one' speaks to journalists. 'Either HHSC changed the first-year budget after its April 7 revision, or the list's "Year 1 subset" is not the same thing as the federal first budget period.' is policy-analyst territory. 'which we did not read' undercuts trust.

sections.heading: How Many Texas Critical Access Hospitals Are on the Rural Texas Strong List?
sections.notes: The payoff section for this reader, buried sixth. Dense: 'Those 86 hospitals appear on 184 applications. The applications hold $132,272,332.34 of first-year money... Of it, $61,803,671.69 sits under 91 signed contracts'. 'Frio Regional may appear under an association whose county column does not match, so we left it out.' Left out of what? The $725,000 / $221,995 Initiative 4 benchmark is genuinely useful. No per-hospital table, so the reader still cannot see their own row.

sections.heading: Does Any Rural Texas Strong Award Pay for Nurses?
sections.notes: Plain, honest answer: the list does not say. 'Budget Period 1' jargon in the Board of Nursing quote.

sections.heading: Does Unsigned Rural Texas Strong Money Have to Be Committed by October 30?
sections.notes: Reader's real question (will my unsigned money vanish Oct 30?) is not answered; the section says HHSC has not said. 'First-year money may not be first-budget-period money.' and 'It could be the Year 1 subset or the full award' both reread. 'as the reconciliation table shows' points to a table never called that. 'subaward' undefined. 'We are not saying any money will be lost.' reads defensive.

sections.heading: What to Do This Week
sections.notes: Concrete and usable. Step 1 'Find your hospital's rows on HHSC's October 23 list' carries no link to the list; the link is back in section 2.
